evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a night scene: a detective parks beside a rain-soaked city street and walks into a noodle shop. Apply the teal-and-orange grade palette.
evals.expected_output: A six-part formula Seedance prompt whose Visual Style slot carries a single teal-and-orange grade sentence with deep teal shadows and rich orange highlights.
expectations: The output contains a single teal-and-orange grade sentence (deep teal shadows, rich orange highlights, warm skin glow).
The grade sentence is placed in the visual style slot, not in the subject or action line.
The output does not mix a second conflicting palette or conflicting color words such as blue-wash or bleach-bypass language.
The output keeps subject and action distinct from the grade sentence.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for an action scene: a courier sprints across a rooftop and leaps to a neighboring fire escape. Apply the bleach-bypass grade.
evals.expected_output: A Seedance prompt whose visual style slot carries the bleach-bypass sentence with hard contrast, blown highlights, and a desaturated silvery sheen.
expectations: The output contains the bleach-bypass grade phrase (hard contrast, blown highlights, desaturated silvery sheen).
The grade sentence sits in the visual style slot and is not duplicated elsewhere.
The output does not stack a second grade direction such as warm-golden or teal-and-orange language.
The action description remains the primary subject of the prompt.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedream prompt for a close-up portrait of a woman laughing at a sidewalk cafe. Use the Kodak Portra 400 film stock look.
evals.expected_output: A structured Seedream prompt with the Kodak Portra 400 film-stock grade sentence inside the Style: section.
expectations: The output places the Portra 400 film-stock grade in the Style: section, not in the Subject or Setting line.
The grade phrase includes soft warm skin tones and gentle low contrast.
The output does not place film-stock words in the subject description.
The output keeps a single grade direction with no conflicting cold or neon language.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a scene of a gardener tending a greenhouse at dusk. I have a style-reference image with a muted palette, soft grain, and diffused highlights — grade the scene off that image.
evals.expected_output: A Seedance prompt that binds the style reference with @Image N syntax and borrows the muted grade language from it in the visual style slot.
expectations: The output binds the style reference with @Image N defines syntax (e.g. @Image 1 defines the color grade).
The output translates the reference into prompt language: muted palette, soft grain, diffused highlights.
The grade language appears in the visual style slot.
The output contains exactly one grade direction and no conflicting palette words.

evals.prompt: I am grading a two-scene project with the cold-steel palette. Write Seedance 2.5 prompts for scene 1 (a lab technician inspecting a sample) and scene 2 (the same technician reviewing a monitor) using the same grade in both.
evals.expected_output: Two Seedance prompts that repeat the identical cold-steel grade phrase in the visual style slot of each scene.
expectations: The exact same cold-steel grade sentence appears in both scene prompts.
Each scene places the grade in its visual style slot.
Neither scene introduces a second or conflicting palette.
The prompts differ only in subject and action, not in grade language.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for the teal-and-orange grade on a two-take scene, and emit the matching FFmpeg filter graph for cross-shot matching in the mix step.
evals.expected_output: A Seedance prompt with the teal-and-orange grade in the visual style slot plus a labeled FFmpeg filter graph for matching only, not a replacement for the prompt grade.
expectations: The output includes the teal-and-orange grade sentence in the visual style slot.
The output emits an ffmpeg -i ... -vf ... command for the teal-and-orange palette.
The output labels the FFmpeg graph as matching-only in the mix step, not as a re-grade of the prompt.
The output does not put FFmpeg commands inside the model prompt text.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedream prompt for a monochrome portrait of an old fisherman with strong facial lines, using the classic black-and-white palette.
evals.expected_output: A Seedream prompt whose Style: section carries the classic B&W grade sentence with explicit tonal-range language (deep blacks, clean whites, silver mid-tones, film grain).
expectations: The output places the grade in the Style: section.
The output uses explicit black-and-white language: deep blacks, bright whites or silver mid-tones, not just 'black and white'.
The output includes a grain or film-texture cue.
The output keeps exactly one grade direction with no color words that contradict monochrome.
